Consult Summary:
- Adult patient with 2 days of gradually worsening constant lower abdominal pain (below umbilicus), feeling hot/sweaty, mild nausea, and pink-tinged urine; empirically treated for possible urinary tract infection (UTI) with trimethoprim; advised pregnancy testing and safety-net follow-up.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Lower abdominal pain (“below belly button”), burning quality, sore to palpation.
- Onset/duration: Started ~2 days ago; gradual onset; progressively worsening.
- Character: Burning, localized below umbilicus; has not spread.
- Severity/impact: Constant but able to function/mobilize.
- Associated urinary symptoms:
  - Pink-tinged urine (possible hematuria; patient unsure).
  - Increased urinary frequency; patient has been drinking more fluids.
  - No dysuria, no stinging, no reported flank pain.
- Gastrointestinal:
  - Constipation last week (now resolved).
  - No diarrhea/loose stools; current bowel movements normal.
  - Mild nausea; no vomiting.
- Constitutional: Feels hot and sweaty; no measured temperature available.
- Gynecologic/sexual:
  - Sexually active with same partner; last intercourse ~4 days ago.
  - Using Implanon (inserted ~1 year ago); still has periods.
  - Last menstrual period reported as “about three weeks ago… two weeks ago” (conflict noted).
  - Last STI screen normal ~6 months ago.
  - Pregnancy not suspected by patient but acknowledged as possible; advised to test.
- Review of systems (pertinent negatives):
  - Respiratory: No shortness of breath, no cough.
  - Cardiac: No palpitations.
  - Neurologic: No headaches, no vision problems.

Past Medical History:
- Medical conditions: None documented.
- Surgical history: None; no prior operations.
- Prior similar symptoms: None.
- Allergies: Not documented.
- Medications:
  - Implanon (etonogestrel implant); dose/route/frequency not documented beyond device in situ.
  - New prescription: Trimethoprim “one tablet twice daily for 3 days” (strength not documented; note conflicting phrasing also mentioned “two tablets”—conflict noted).
  - PRN advice: Paracetamol for pain (dose/route/frequency not documented).

Social History:
- Living situation: Share house with two roommates.
- Occupation: Accountant; currently working.
- Tobacco: Does not smoke.
- Alcohol: Drinks socially; not above typical social use per patient.
- Substance use: Not documented.

Family History:
- No known family history relevant to bowel conditions; no other relevant family history reported.

Physical Examination:
- Not documented.

Investigations:
- None performed at this visit.
- Tests were discussed to help determine cause; patient opted for empirical antibiotics first.
- Pregnancy test: Advised to perform to rule out pregnancy.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Lower abdominal pain with urinary symptoms; possible UTI with hematuria; differential includes gastrointestinal cause and pregnancy-related etiology.
  - Empiric antibiotics: Trimethoprim prescribed; instruction given as “one tablet twice daily for 3 days” (strength not documented; initial mention of “two tablets” also made—conflict noted).
  - Symptomatic care: Paracetamol as needed; maintain hydration; optional cranberry juice.
  - Safety net: Seek care if worsening abdominal pain, persistent/high fevers or feeling very hot/sweaty, vomiting, or new/worsening symptoms.
  - Follow-up: Reassess in a few days if not improving or sooner if worsening.
- Issue 2: Pregnancy not excluded.
  - Plan: Perform home or clinic pregnancy test; contact clinician with results. If positive or if pain worsens, urgent evaluation advised.
- Issue 3: Recent constipation, now resolved.
  - No active intervention; monitor bowel habits.

General plan items:
- Consider urinalysis and urine culture, and further evaluation (including abdominal/pelvic exam and labs) if symptoms persist or worsen, or if pregnancy test is positive.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Vitals; allergy status; medication list reconciliation (including doses/strengths); abdominal and pelvic examination; urinalysis/urine culture; pain severity score; pregnancy test result.
- Internal conflicts:
  - LMP reported as “about three weeks ago” then “two weeks ago.”
  - Antibiotic instructions included both “two tablets” and “one tablet twice daily for 3 days.”
  - Patient addressed as “Tim” and later as “Kim.”
  - Hematuria uncertain (“pink urine,” patient unsure if blood).
- Transcript quality: Generally clear; minor hesitations and brief contradictions as noted.
